Expected output SHAPE for s07-file-edit-diff.

The demo (`go run .` with no flags) is fully offline and deterministic: it seeds a
temp file, applies a two-block SEARCH/REPLACE diff, prints the before/after, then
replays the SAME diff in growing chunks to show streamed application. There is no
LLM and no network, so this output IS reproducible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ GOWORK=off go run .
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
== original main.go ==
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	fmt.Println("hello")
}

== diff (SEARCH/REPLACE blocks) ==
------- SEARCH
func main() {
=======
func greeting() string { return "hello, cline" }

func main() {
+++++++ REPLACE
------- SEARCH
	fmt.Println("hello")
=======
	fmt.Println(greeting())
+++++++ REPLACE

== edited main.go ==
package main

import "fmt"

func greeting() string { return "hello, cline" }

func main() {
	fmt.Println(greeting())
}

== streamed application (incremental result length) ==
  after  1/12 diff lines: result is 0 bytes
  after  3/12 diff lines: result is 28 bytes
  after  5/12 diff lines: result is 78 bytes
  after  7/12 diff lines: result is 92 bytes
  after  9/12 diff lines: result is 92 bytes
  after 11/12 diff lines: result is 117 bytes
  final result == one-shot result: true

Notes:
- Two blocks apply in file order: the first inserts greeting() above main(), the
  second rewrites the Println call. The applier walks the original forward, so
  blocks MUST be in the order they appear in the file.
- The streamed run feeds growing prefixes of the diff; the in-progress result
  length only ever grows, and the final streamed result equals the one-shot one.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ GOWORK=off go test -count=1 ./...
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ok  	learn-cline/s07	0.50s
